svg.text: Convex and Non-Convex Problems: When Can a Local Minimum Be Trusted?
• Every chord lies on or above the curve
• Some chord falls below the curve
• A local minimum can be a TRAP
Hillier & Lieberman example (non-convex feasible region): local max (4, 3) gives Z = 27, global max (0, 7) gives Z = 35
